sentences.text:
This is an application under Section 439 Cr.P.C.
2.

The petitioner is an accused in connection with Naugaon P.S. Case No.119 of 2024 corresponding to G.R. Case No.829 of 2024 for the offences under Sections 452/376/511 of the I.P.C. pending in the Court of the learned S.D.J.M., Jagatsinghpur.
The petitioner had approached before the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Jagatsinghpur praying for grant of bail.
The learned Court below vide its order dated 17.05.2024 rejected the bail application of the petitioner.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 439 Cr.P.C. praying for enlargement on bail.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on instruction from the petitioner, submits that, except the present bail application, no other bail application of the petitioner is pending in any other Court relating to the aforesaid F.I.R.
4.

The prosecution case in short is that, on 04.05.2024 at about 2.30 A.M., while the informant was sleeping in her house along with her daughter, the petitioner entered her house and made an attempt to rape her.
When her daughter wake-up, the petitioner fled away from the spot.

Hence, the F.I.R.
5.
The statement of the prosecutrix, who is about 30 years old was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.

She in her statement has stated that on 04.05.2024 at about 2.30 P.M., the present petitioner came to her house when she was sleeping with her daughter and the petitioner attempted to commit sexual act on her.
The prosecutrix subsequently was asked for medical examination, to which she has refused.

Perusal of the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., it Sashikanta Das @ Duduna vs State Of Odisha .... Opposite Party(S) on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19475154/
1 also reveals that there is no allegation of sexual intercourse caused by the petitioner rather the petitioner alleged to have attempted to commit the sexual act.

sentences.text: 6. Regard being had to the period of custody from 07.05.2024 and the nature of accusation, I am inclined to admit the petitioner on bail.

Hence, the petitioner is directed to be released on bail by the Court in seisin over the matter in the aforesaid case on such terms and conditions as it would deem just and proper, subject to the following additional conditions:-
(i) The petitioner shall appear before the trial Court on each date of hearing without fail.
(ii) He shall not tamper with the evidence in any manner whatsoever.

(iii) He shall not keep contact with the victim and her family members in any manner whatsoever In the event, the petitioner is found wanting for violation of any of the bail conditions imposed by this Court or the trial Court even on a single occasion, the prosecution is at liberty to move appropriate application before the Court below for cancellation of the concession of bail granted by this Court.
If such application is filed, the trial Court should decide the application on its own merit.
7. The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
